chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Ismail, from his father who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man to whom death presented itself, so he bequeathed to his son and two brothers. The son witnessed his bequest and the two brothers were absent. So when it was after a few days they both refused to accept the executorship in fear that his son would pounce upon the two of them, and they would not be able to act with what is befitting. So a cousin of theirs guaranteed to them both, and that he would be obedient among them, and that he would suffice for the two of them from his son. So they both entered into it with this condition, but his son did not suffice for the two of them, and it had been stipulated upon his son, and they both said, 'We are free from the executorship, and we are excused from neglecting the entirety of the matters and exiting from it.' Is it correct for both of them that they absolve themselves from what was in their hands and come out from it?
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is necessary for you to join upon whichever aspect it was, for you would be recompensed, perhaps that would resolve (the matters) with his son.'

key_terms.الْخُرُوجِ: Exiting or being released from liability

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an executor accepts a bequest with a condition that they are not liable if the heir fails to cooperate?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the legal principle of 'shart al-khurooj' (condition of exit) is validated, demonstrating that an executor can be released from liability if the primary beneficiary fails to perform duties, provided the condition was explicitly agreed upon. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contractual freedom and the practical flexibility in managing inheritance to prevent conflict, ensuring the executor is not held accountable for the son's potential misconduct.
